- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: security_pass_fix_reissue_exhausted (lines ~4776-4814), security_pass_handle_failed_fix_issue close branches (lines ~5038-5047)
  Problem: When `gh issue close` fails persistently on a cap-exhausted or re-issue predecessor, the function warns and returns 0 with state untouched. The predecessor issue remains open with `ai:orchestrator-managed` still attached, and `security_pass_active_fix_issues` still points at it. The next poll tick re-enters `security_pass_handle_failed_fix_issue` → `security_pass_fix_reissue_exhausted` again and loops forever emitting `::warning::Could not close exhausted security-pass fix issue #<n>` every 5 minutes. Worse, if an operator later comments `/re-security-pass`, `create_security_pass_fix_issue` would dedupe on the open managed issue (it filters only by `state=open` + `labels=ai:orchestrator-managed` + tracking/local-id markers) and re-adopt the dead predecessor, re-entering the same cap-exhausted loop on the next audit cycle.
  Why it fails at runtime: A persistent close failure (e.g. token scope revoked, repo archived, label-protected issues) creates a tight unbounded retry loop with no Telegram alert and no automatic terminalization. The "next poll retries" comment acknowledges the risk but does not bound it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

  location: security_pass_fix_reissue_exhausted (≈ lines 4787-4799) and the two `gh issue close` blocks in security_pass_handle_failed_fix_issue (≈ lines 5038-5047)
  issue: When close succeeds (or fails), the issue keeps `ai:orchestrator-managed` so `create_security_pass_fix_issue` dedupe on the next `/re-security-pass` can re-adopt the dead predecessor. Removing the managed label alongside the terminal label flip prevents that re-adoption and breaks the persistent-close-failure loop.
  suggested minimal fix: Append `--remove-label 'ai:orchestrator-managed'` to the `gh issue edit` calls (or do it before the close call so the close call itself isn't blocked by label-protection). Worst case also surface a CRITICAL tg_notify on the persistent-close-failure branch so operators see the stall, not just `::warning::` lines.
  estimated lines changed: 2-4
